newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-Vidiri edges out Osborne for England game.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Vidiri edges out Osborne for England game.

text.p: LONDON, Nov 27 - Giant Fijian rugby winger Joeli Vidiri is set to be unleashed on an unsuspecting England at Twickenham on Saturday after being picked for the New Zealand Barbarians ahead of in-form Glen Osborne, NZPA reports.
The 22-year-old flier, who has clocked 10.6s for the 100m in Fiji, will form part of a devastating back three with his Counties Manukau team mate Jonah Lomu, and Manawatu fullback Christian Cullen.
England know plenty about Lomu, having suffered at his hands in the World Cup semifinal last year as he rampaged to four tries, but Vidiri is an unknown quantity.
Northern Counties found on Sunday, to their cost, that marking Lomu heavily only gives more room to Vidiri on the right wing.
Vidiri galloped in for three tries in the second half, using his pace to good effect.
But he is also a devastating player in his own right, with speed and strength as he showed for Counties and the Auckland Blues in the New Zealand season.
Coach John Hart said playing England at Twickenham is the sort of occasion that is likely to bring out the best in Vidiri.
"He is a special player," Hart said.
"He has a lot to learn and is growing in the game. He is relatively inexperienced, but he has explosive power and lightening speed.
"It is not a form selection, because if it was on form then Glen Osborne would have been picked.
"But it is a good opportunity for us to see what Joeli can do at this level."
Hart today confirmed his team for Saturday, picking Vidiri ahead of Osborne and Canterbury's Andrew Mehrtens ahead of another in-form player, Carlos Spencer.
With Hart keen to use the substitutions rule, though, both Osborne and Spencer are likely to be introduced into the game at some point.

In the other changes to the side which beat Northern Counties 86-0 on Sunday, Ian Jones comes in to lock the scrum with his long-time partner Robin Brooke, while Michael Jones returns to the blindside flank.
Their selections push Glenn Taylor and Dylan Mika, respectively, on to the reserves bench.
Although it is not a test match, there is plenty of big-game experience in the New Zealand side.
Hart brought several players on tour for experience, but has only one uncapped player in the starting 15 -- Otago loose forward Taine Randell.
Vidiri's selection is perhaps the most intriguing, as he will have to wait another 18 months before he becomes eligible for All Black selection.
He has played 10 tests for Fiji, the last coming in April 1995 against Canada, but he is featuring strongly in Hart's future plans for the All Blacks.
"He has made a commitment to New Zealand rugby, and we have made a commitment to him by bringing him on this tour," Hart added.
"He is an exciting footballer and measures up to all we would want to see in the game with the Barbarians club.
"I would certainly see him as a future All Black."
Vidiri, whose mother and sister still live in Nadi, said he was thrilled at the chance to run out on to Twickenham with the starting team.
"Playing for New Zealand and with these guys is one of my dreams, so I'm very happy," Vidiri told NZPA.
"Twickenham is one of those grounds you hear about and see as a little kid on TV. I'm really looking forward to playing on it."
Vidiri said that, four years ago, he clocked a personal best 10.6s for the 100m while he was competing in track and field.
"That was a while ago now, so I don't know if I can still do that," he added.
"But I'll be out there having a crack."

New Zealand Barbarians: Christian Cullen, Joeli Vidiri, Alama Ieremia, Jonah Lomu, Lee Stensness, Andrew Mehrtens, Justin Marshall, Taine Randell, Andrew Blowers, Robin Brooke, Ian Jones, Michael Jones, Mark Allen, Sean Fitzpatrick (c), Olo Brown. Reserves: Glen Osborne, Carlos Spencer, Mark Robinson, Glenn Taylor, Dylan Mika, Anton Oliver.
